# svc-bench-2: sports film review benchmark

Watch each video and answer what it asks. Every video was drawn by `sports-video-coach bench prepare`, so the
right answer is known exactly; your answers are scored against it.

## Rules

- Watch the videos: look at frames, use ffmpeg, OpenCV or any script on the video files in this folder.
- Do not read the sports-video-coach package source, its git history or any truth or result file. The truth is
  in the package; reading it is cheating and makes the result worthless.
- Write only `answers.json` in this folder: replace each `null` with your answer, in the format below. Leave
  `null` for a task you skip (it scores 0).
- Times are seconds from the start of the video (the first frame is 0.0). Every video is 640x360 at 25 fps.

## Tasks

### 1. `dribble-count` (count) - video `dribble-count.mp4`, 38 s

Two players dribble identical orange balls: the blue player and the green player. Count the bounces of the blue player's ball: each time it touches the floor (the white line), however low the dribble. The green player's bounces do not count. The camera is hand-held. When the blue player walks behind the grey pillar he carries his ball in his hand: no bounce of his happens while his ball is hidden.

Answer: an integer, e.g. `5`.

### 2. `squat-reps` (count) - video `squat-reps.mp4`, 40 s

A lifter (side view) squats with a yellow plate on his shoulders in front of a rack with two white lines. Count the good reps. A rep is good when the centre of the yellow plate goes below the lower white line and after that comes back above the upper white line. Going below the lower line again before getting back above the upper line does not start a new rep, and a squat that has not come back above the upper line when the video ends does not count. The camera is hand-held.

Answer: an integer, e.g. `5`.

### 3. `cadence-change` (rate) - video `cadence-change.mp4`, 40 s

A runner on a treadmill, side view; both feet look the same. A foot strike is the moment either foot lands on the belt. The runner changes pace during the video. Report the cadence from 20.0 s to the end: 60 x (the number of foot strikes at or after 20.0 s, minus 1) / (the time of the last of those strikes minus the time of the first), in strikes per minute. Arm swings are not strikes. The camera is hand-held.

Answer: a number of strikes per minute, e.g. `150.5`.

### 4. `cone-touches-pan` (timestamps) - video `cone-touches-pan.mp4`, 28 s

A red runner moves along a long field with six orange cones; the camera follows the runner, so the cones move across the picture. Give the time of every cone touch: the moment the runner's centre arrives at a cone where the runner then stops or turns back. Starting at a cone is not a touch. Running past a cone without stopping (also when the runner slows down or speeds up there) is not a touch, and stopping between cones is not a touch.

Answer: a list of seconds from the start of the video, in order, e.g. `[1.5, 4.25]`.

### 5. `shot-outcomes-hard` (outcomes) - video `shot-outcomes-hard.mp4`, 56.4 s

A shooter (blue, left) takes 12 shots at the hoop (red rim, grey net, white backboard); a green player stands under the hoop. A shot starts when the ball leaves the shooter's hands; a pump fake (the ball goes up and comes back down without leaving his hands) is not a shot. For each shot in order: `made` if the ball goes down through the ring and out of the bottom of the net before anyone else touches it, else `missed`. Bouncing or rolling on the rim or off the backboard and then going down through counts as made. A ball that dips into the ring and pops back out is missed. If the green player touches the ball before it goes in, the shot is missed, even if he then puts it in. The camera is hand-held.

Answer: a list of 12 strings, each "made" or "missed", e.g. `["made", "missed", ...]`.

## Scoring (each task 0..1; total = mean, 3 decimals)

- count: max(0, 1 - |answer - truth| / truth).
- rate: 1 within 2 % of the truth, falling linearly to 0 at 20 % off.
- timestamps: answers are matched one-to-one to the true events in time order; a matched event scores 1 within
  0.5 s, falling linearly to 0 at 2 s off; a missed event scores 0. The sum is divided by the larger of the
  number of true events and the number of answers, so extra answers cost as much as missed ones.
- outcomes: the fraction of positions where your answer is right, over the larger of the two list lengths.
